correctness.rationale: Every threshold MIS is either the complete set of zero creation vertices or one creation-one plus subsequent zeros. Queries are one-hot or prefix, yielding \(\operatorname{VCdim}=1\) and an exact recurrence. A depth-\(h\) tree requires \(2^h\) hypotheses and \(2^{h-1}-1\) distinct noninitial prefix cuts, establishing \(n\ge3\cdot2^{h-1}-1\). The unique word \(01(011)^{2^{h-1}-1}\) supplies perfectly balanced prefix cuts and final pair splits; equality forces its cut positions. Explicit finite enumeration corroborates independent premises for 2,047 words through eleven vertices, with no claim that finite checks prove all orders.

value.rationale: The sharp minimum graph order and unique extremal realization are natural structural invariants of a graph-constrained online membership-learning problem, rather than an arbitrary slice of a numerical table. The distinct-cut argument explains a genuine extra resource beyond the cardinality lower bound; it is quantitative, exact at all depths, and computes exact rank from creation sequences in cubic time. The VC dimension remains one, so it locates the precise onset of each online-shattering rank within a classical hereditary graph class.
